newsitem.title: UK: Film posters worth more at auction as time goes by.
newsitem.headline: Film posters worth more at auction as time goes by.

text.p: A film poster for "Casablanca," the war-time cinema classic starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman, sold for 23,000 pounds ($38,010) at British auction house Christie's on Tuesday.

The film opened in 1942, only three weeks after World War Two allies landed in Casablanca, Morocco, and is considered one of the most romantic films ever made with its haunting theme "As Time Goes By."
"Casablanca" was one of the top lots from a collection of classic posters from 1900 to 1974 formed by Stanley Caidin, an American entertainment lawyer.
"Frankenstein" (1931) made 14,950 pounds and "The Birth of a Nation" (1915), the cinema's first epic, went for 10,350 pounds.
"The Kid" (1921), starring Charlie Chaplin fetched 13,800 pounds, and the poster for Walt Disney's "Pinocchio" (1940) sold for 4,370 pounds.
Caidin began collecting in the mid-1970s and over a period of 12 years put together one of the largest single owner collections of rare and museum quality posters. ($1=.6050 Pound)
